tool.name: FAIRe mapper: propose mapping
tool.description: match the columns of a sample sheet to FAIRe terms
tool.command: mkdir out && python '$__tool_directory__/faire_mapper.py' map @TABLE_ARGS@ --checklist '$__tool_directory__/checklist/FAIRe_checklist_v1.0.2.xlsx' #if str($assay_type) != 'any': --assay_type '$assay_type' #end if #if $sample_types: --sample_types '$sample_types' #end if #if $responses: --responses '$responses' #end if #if $dictionary: --dictionary '$dictionary' #if str($dictionary_sheet).strip(): --dictionary_sheet '$dictionary_sheet' #end if #end if --shortlist $shortlist --shortlist_close $shortlist_close $other_terms --outdir out

param.name: assay_type
param.label: Assay type
param.help: Leaves out the FAIRe terms that only apply to the other assay type.

param.name: sample_types
param.label: Sample types
param.help: Leaves out the FAIRe fields specific to other sample types. Tick none to consider all.

param.name: responses
param.label: Answers for columns to review (optional)
param.help: A JSON list of decisions from a reviewer or a language model, for example [{"column": "habitat", "term": "env_broad_scale"}, {"column": "notes", "term": null}]. These columns are fixed first and the rest are matched around them.

param.name: dictionary
param.label: Data dictionary (optional)
param.help: What each column holds: a table with a column name, a description and units (for example columns headed Variable, Description, Units), or a README with one line per column, such as 'Days frozen: number of days the water was frozen before filtering'. Lines and rows that name no column of the table are ignored.

param.name: dictionary_sheet
param.label: Excel sheet of the data dictionary
param.help: Leave empty for the first sheet.

param.name: other_terms
param.label: Suggest MIxS or Darwin Core terms for columns with no FAIRe term
param.help: As the FAIRe guidelines ask. Each suggestion is for review: once you confirm it in the crosswalk, apply mapping names the column after the term.

param.name: shortlist_close
param.label: Candidate terms listed when no term clearly leads
param.help: Used when the last of the candidates above scores within 0.1 of the first. Set it to the same number as above to always list that many.

tool.help:
@EARLY_VERSION@ **What it does**
This tool proposes which FAIRe term each column of your table holds, so you do not have to rename columns by hand. The result is a **crosswalk**: a table with one row for each column of your table and the FAIRe term it matches, saved in SSSOM, a standard format for such tables. You check and correct the crosswalk, most easily in the **review sheet** it also writes, and **FAIRe mapper: apply mapping** then uses it to write your FAIRe workbook.
For every column, the tool scores each FAIRe term on three kinds of evidence:
- **the header**, which it compares with the term's name and its common alternative names (for example *Lat*, *Collection date* or *Primer F seq*); - **the values**, which it compares with what the term should hold: its type, format and allowed values (for example latitudes, ISO dates, primer sequences, or *sample* and *negative control*); - **the level**: a column with the same value on every row, such as the primer sequence, suits a term that applies to the whole project or assay.
Each FAIRe term is given to one column at most. The tool then routes each column to one of these outcomes, shown in the *route* column of the mapping report:
- **accept**: a strong match, clearly ahead of the alternatives; - **review**: a plausible match that a person should check, listed with the alternatives; - **no match**: no FAIRe term fits well enough (the column is kept under its own name, as a user-defined field, unless apply mapping is set to leave such columns out); - **confirmed**: a match set by a person in your answers file; - **model**: a match chosen by a language model in your answers file (answers marked ``"by": "model:..."``). Check these, because only a person can confirm a match.
Some columns fill more than one term, and each term then has its own row in the crosswalk. Examples are a number and its unit in one cell ("1 L"), latitude and longitude in one cell (MIxS lat_lon, "40.57 S 148.73 E"), and a single depth for each sample, which fills both minimumDepthInMeters and maximumDepthInMeters. A yes/no column that says which samples are controls, under a header such as *Control_Neg*, is matched to samp_category, with yes written as *negative control* and no as *sample*. Empty columns are not matched.
**MIxS and Darwin Core terms for columns with no FAIRe term.** The FAIRe guidelines ask for a MIxS or Darwin Core term, where one exists, before a made-up name. For a column with no FAIRe match, the tool looks for one whose name matches the column's, and adds it to the crosswalk for review, with its own identifier (*MIXS:0000505* for phosphate, *dwc:verbatimDepth*). The terms come with the tool (``mixs_dwc_terms.tsv``), so Galaxy needs no web access: 745 MIxS terms (v7.0.1) and 95 Darwin Core terms (the record-level, Event, Location and MaterialEntity terms of Simple Darwin Core) that FAIRe does not have. Every word of the column's name must match the term's name, or be a common word such as *sample*: *Phosphate (uM)* gets MIxS phosphate, *Ammonia* gets ammonium (close, so check it), and *Field bottle number* gets nothing, although Darwin Core has fieldNumber. Once you confirm a row, apply mapping names the column after the term. For a MIxS number, which MIxS writes with its unit (0.7 micromole per liter), it adds the unit from the column name, in brackets at its end, to each value. Untick *Suggest MIxS or Darwin Core terms* to leave them out.
@HELP_INPUTS@
-----
**Inputs**
- **Your table**, as an Excel file or as text separated by commas, semicolons or tabs, and the row that holds its headers. Comment lines starting with # above the headers, as in NCBI and ENA submission sheets, are skipped. The tool reads text in Latin-1 or Windows encodings and decimal commas (0,45) correctly, and the *summary* output records how it read the file. - **The assay type and sample types**, so the tool can leave out FAIRe terms that do not apply. - **Answers for the columns to review** (optional), as a JSON list such as ``[{"column": "habitat", "term": "env_broad_scale"}, {"column": "notes", "term": null}]``. The answers can come from a person, or from **FAIRe mapper: ask a language model** given the *columns to review* output. Answers from a model should carry ``"by": "model:<name>"``, so that they are not shown as confirmed. Run the tool again with the answers, and it matches the rest of the table around them. - **Data dictionary** (optional): a description of what each column holds, as a table (column name, description and units) or as a README with one line per column (``Days frozen: number of days the water was frozen before filtering``). The tool treats a description like a header, so a FAIRe term that the description names gets support from it. When the description names other terms but not the one the header matched, the header match counts for less: for example, *Sample processing* described as "the person that filtered the sample" points to recordedBy. Units in a description ("in litres", "(µm)") are used like units in a header. The descriptions are also passed to the model in the *columns to review*.
**Outputs**
- **mapping report**: one row for each column, giving the proposed term, its FAIRe sheet, the route, the score and the evidence. It also gives hints for reformatting (for example converting dd/mm/yyyy dates, or a unit found in a header), the shortlist of candidates (five, or ten when no term clearly leads), how columns combine or split, the column's description from the data dictionary, and, for a column with no FAIRe term, the MIxS or Darwin Core term suggested (*other_standard*). - **review sheet** (Excel): the matches laid out for a person to review, one row per column: the input term (the column heading), the proposed FAIRe term (or a MIxS or Darwin Core term when no FAIRe term fits), its score, the mapper's call (accept, review or no match), the mapper's reasoning, the reviewer's decision (Accept, Reject or Change, from a drop-down), the replacement FAIRe term (a drop-down with the column's best candidates first, a blank line, then every FAIRe term) and what the column is kept as if the match is rejected (its own term). Rows to review are shaded. Hover over a proposed term to see its definition. It also has the additional checks to make and how to review. Give it to **FAIRe mapper: apply mapping** as the crosswalk once the decisions are made. - **crosswalk (SSSOM)**: the proposed and confirmed matches in the `SSSOM <https://mapping-commons.github.io/sssom/>`_ format, which you can reuse with later datasets. - **mandatory terms not covered**: the FAIRe mandatory terms that no column provides. It leaves out the terms that the tool's settings supply (the assay type and checklist version) and those that apply only to the other assay type. Many of these are project-level values usually found in the methods text, and the rest are questions to ask the data provider. - **columns to review**: the review and no-match columns, with their values and candidate terms, in a form that a reviewer or a language model can answer. - **additional checks to make**: what only a person can decide before applying the mapping, each with what to do about it: a sample name used on more than one row; sample names that read as controls (*Filtration control 1 + 2*, *Extbl19_4*) when no column says which rows are controls; columns with values only in the first rows, which may be notes about the whole study; and times of collection (the column matched to verbatimEventTime or eventDate) with no time zone, or in UTC only (daily cycles follow local time); and columns matched to FAIRe terms that people often confuse (the sampling depth and the depth of the water column, the volume collected and the volume extracted, the taxa the primers amplify and the taxa the study set out to detect), with how to tell them apart. The tool lists these and changes nothing. The list has only its header row when there is nothing to decide. - **summary**: the number of columns in each route, and the number with a MIxS or Darwin Core term (*other_standard*).
-----
**How accurate is it?**
We tested the tool on tables built from a real FAIRe dataset, with headers written independently in six lab styles. The first choice was correct for 81 to 93% of columns, and the correct term was in the shortlist for 94 to 99%. Of the columns routed to *accept*, 98 to 100% were correct. Matching on values alone, with headers that give nothing away, is much weaker (about 24%). The tests covered commonly used fields, and less common FAIRe fields are likely to match less well.
Four published eDNA datasets were harder: the first choice was right for 55% of the columns that have a FAIRe term, and 84% of accepted columns were right. A data dictionary helps. On two test tables described column by column, the first choice rose from 81% to 91% and from 90% to 94%. Treat *review* columns as suggestions, and check the accepted ones too.
